note: Seeded overlap CANDIDATES only. A pair here is a starting point for detection, never a verdict: verdicts live in the committed store (docs/native-surfaces/records.json by default) and are human-gated. Adding a pair here proposes a row; it does not create one.

pairs.why: Both review a diff or a PR for correctness findings; the names collide outright.
Both clean up changed code without changing behavior.
Same cleanup job at batch scale across many files.
Both produce a security-focused review of a change; the extraction reports the native side under plugin_backed, not builtin_commands.
Both launch the project's app to see a change actually working.
Both look at the health of a Claude Code installation.
Both diagnose a slow or unhealthy install; doctor also offers to fix.
Both assemble an operator morning view. Session-provided, so it is observation-only: absent from the vendored binary's bundled set.
clean-stop, handoff, and retro suggest the built-in /export at session-end moments; the command is the only stable conversation-export surface and the skills reference it by name.
Both can answer 'show me this visually'; the first-party plugin's interactive explorer with a prompt round-trip overlaps visualize's rich-page medium.
Both build a browser page with switchable controls; explore-directions varies your project's own UI while a playground explores an arbitrary parameter space.
visualize already routes hand-tweakable layouts to the bundled design canvas; the live integration deserves a recorded verdict.
explore-directions offers the design-canvas Artifact as one of its mockup surfaces; same live integration, sibling component.
The design-sync family (sync, consent, revoke, login) is registered in the binary near the canvas skill visualize gates; recorded to rule on, not to integrate.
